title: Corpus storage: a corpus that pins its own dimension, and chunks excluded from the article corpus by construction
background: loopctl already stores dimension-tagged vectors well: article_embeddings uses an unconstrained vector column with an explicit dim discriminator and a vector_dims(embedding) = dim CHECK (priv/repo/migrations/20260721000100_create_embedding_side_tables.exs), and per-dimension HNSW indexes are built from one single-sourced SQL generator (lib/loopctl/repo/hnsw_index.ex) over Loopctl.Embeddings.supported_dimensions/0, currently [768, 1024, 1536]. What it does not have is anywhere to put a VERBATIM document chunk. The corpus tier needs three tables and one decision that the originating issue did not make: where the embedding dimension is pinned. Loopctl.Embeddings.active_dimension/1 resolves a dimension per TENANT, and the 20260721000300 migration pinned it deliberately so the stored corpus's actual shape, not a mutable model setting, is authoritative. A tenant whose article corpus is pinned at 1536 will index a document corpus with a LOCAL 768-dimension model, and both must coexist in the same tenant at the same time. Reading the tenant pin for a corpus makes the epic's first consumer unimplementable.

story.as_a: an agent maintaining a reference-document corpus that lives in its own repo
story.i_want_to: have loopctl store verbatim chunks and their vectors in tables of their own, with the corpus pinning its own embedding model and dimension
story.so_that: a local 768-dimension model can index my documents without disturbing the tenant's 1536-dimension article corpus, and those chunks can never leak into recall

rationale: Two structural decisions carry the whole epic, and both belong in the storage layer where they cannot be argued with later. First, dimension is a property of the CORPUS, not the tenant: pinning it at creation and refusing to change it makes a mixed-dimension tenant ordinary rather than exceptional. Second, chunks live in their own tables, so exclusion from recall, heat, novelty and consolidation is a consequence of the schema rather than a policy any future change could forget to apply.

acceptance_criteria.description: A `corpora` table exists with tenant_id (NOT NULL, FK to tenants, ON DELETE CASCADE), project_id (nullable FK), slug, name, description, mode (enum: server_embedded | client_embedded), embedding_model (text), dim (integer, NOT NULL, CHECK dim > 0), allow_snippets (boolean, NOT NULL, with NO DDL default), and timestamps. (tenant_id, slug) is unique. allow_snippets carries no column default deliberately: it is TRUE for a server_embedded corpus (loopctl holds the text already) and FALSE for a client_embedded one (the privacy-preserving default US-43.3 AC-43.3.6 states), and a mode-conditional default is expressible in the changeset but not in DDL. THIS story's changeset supplies it from mode, so US-43.2's create cannot insert a NULL before US-43.3 lands.

A `document_chunks` table exists with tenant_id, corpus_id (FK, ON DELETE CASCADE), source_ref (text, NOT NULL — a repo-relative path or URL), locator (jsonb — page, byte range, or heading path; the shape is the client's, loopctl only stores and returns it), text (nullable — NULL is the mode B state), snippet (nullable), content_hash (text, NOT NULL), ordinal (integer) and timestamps. The keyword lane's FTS column and index belong to US-43.2, which owns that lane and its regconfig decision. A unique index on (corpus_id, source_ref, locator) — content_hash is NOT in the key — is what makes corpus_index idempotent. content_hash is an ordinary column compared against the incoming chunk to decide unchanged vs replaced; putting it in the key would let a chunk whose text moved insert a SECOND row at the same locator instead of replacing the first, which is exactly what US-43.2 AC-43.2.3 forbids.

A `document_chunk_embeddings` table mirrors article_embeddings exactly in shape and constraint set, and its columns are named EXACTLY tenant_id, dim, embedding and live_denorm: those four names are what let the schema-parameterized query builder Loopctl.Knowledge.VectorSearch.index_safe_dimension_knn_base/6 be reused unchanged. It carries tenant_id, document_chunk_id (FK, ON DELETE CASCADE), dim (integer, CHECK dim > 0), embedding (UNCONSTRAINED vector), live_denorm (boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true), embedding_content_hash, timestamps, a CONSTRAINT document_chunk_embeddings_dim_matches_vector CHECK (vector_dims(embedding) = dim), and a unique index on (tenant_id, document_chunk_id, dim). live_denorm carries NO TRIGGER and is never written false: a chunk has no supersession state, so the PL/pgSQL trigger pair article_embeddings needs has nothing to mirror. The COLUMN is still required — HnswIndex.create_dimension_index_sql/2 emits WHERE dim = N AND live_denorm, and maybe_live_denorm_only/2 adds the matching query predicate — so dropping it would fork both the index SQL and the query builder. A comment in the migration records that the column is load-bearing for index reuse and deliberately inert, so nobody later removes it as dead.

The corpus's dim MUST be in Loopctl.Embeddings.supported_dimensions/0 at creation time, rejected with a named error otherwise, because a dimension outside that set has no pre-built HNSW index and index DDL is migration-plane only. The rejection message names the supported set and states why (the same reason .well-known/loopctl publishes it).

Per-dimension partial HNSW expression indexes are created on document_chunk_embeddings for every value of Loopctl.Embeddings.supported_dimensions/0 using Loopctl.Repo.HnswIndex.create_dimension_index_sql/2 — the SAME generator the article and memory side tables use, so the cast expression stays CHARACTER-IDENTICAL between the index and the query (the planner cannot match them otherwise) and the build parameters m and ef_construction cannot drift between tiers. The new table is ADDED to HnswIndex's @side_tables list, so the missing_dimension_indexes/1 drift guard covers it — a dimension published in config but never index-built makes every read at that dimension seq-scan the corpus, which is the #170/#172 class of outage. The migration uses CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY with @disable_ddl_transaction and @disable_migration_lock, matching 20260721000200, and is a SEPARATE file from the table creation.

All three tables ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY via Loopctl.Repo.RlsHelpers.enable_rls/1 (not FORCE — the production role owns the tables without BYPASSRLS), and each has a tenant isolation test proving tenant A cannot read tenant B's corpora, chunks or chunk embeddings through Loopctl.Repo.

This story adds NO heavy or vector read — the first is US-43.2 corpus_search — so what is asserted here is the CONTRACT the new schemas must be able to satisfy when that read arrives, rather than a property of code this story ships. A query joining document_chunks to document_chunk_embeddings must be able to carry x.tenant_id == ^tenant_id on the from source AND on every joined source, which is what Loopctl.HeavyRead's conjunctive predicate guard demands; guard!/2 is private, so TC-43.1.7 asserts it through the only reachable path — HeavyRead.all/2 accepts the fully scoped join and raises ArgumentError (not fully scoped to the given tenant) on the variant scoping only the from source, exactly as test/loopctl/embeddings_side_table_reads_test.exs:310-328 already does, so a schema that made the join un-scopeable fails here and not in US-43.2. The existing heavy_read_guard_test.exs build guard (no lib/ module may reach HeavyReadRepo directly) keeps passing.

A GUARD TEST asserts the exclusion the epic depends on: no query built by the recall path, knowledge_heat_index, novelty scoring or the consolidation pass reads document_chunks or document_chunk_embeddings. It is anchored to code rather than prose — it inspects the modules those paths are built from for a reference to the new schemas and fails on any — and it asserts its own matched set is non-empty so it cannot go vacuous if a module is renamed.

Deleting a corpus cascades to its chunks and their embeddings in one statement, leaving no orphans; a test inserts a corpus with chunks and embeddings, deletes the corpus row, and asserts zero rows remain in both child tables. Cascade is declared in the DDL, not implemented in application code.

Loopctl.Corpus context module exposes create_corpus/2, get_corpus/2, list_corpora/2, delete_corpus/2, upsert_chunks/3 and delete_chunks_for_source/3, every one taking tenant_id as its first argument, with tenant_id never in a changeset cast. No HTTP surface is added in this story — the API and MCP tools are US-43.2 and US-43.4.

Neither Loopctl.Embeddings.active_dimension/1 NOR resolve_write_dimension/1 is called anywhere on the corpus path, and a test asserts the Corpus modules reference neither. active_dimension/1 resolves per TENANT and would silently return 1536 for a 768 corpus. resolve_write_dimension/1 is worse than wrong: it PINS tenants.tenant_embedding_dimension and tenant_embedding_model as a side effect, so one corpus write by a tenant that had not yet embedded an article would pin that tenant's ARTICLE corpus to the local document model. The corpus's own dim is read from the corpus row and from nowhere else.

document_chunks and document_chunk_embeddings are append-heavy and get the same autovacuum tuning the existing embedding tables carry (autovacuum_analyze_scale_factor 0.05, autovacuum_vacuum_insert_scale_factor 0.1, per migration 20260804230000). This matters more here than for articles: a corpus re-index rewrites whole documents at once, so dead tuples arrive in bursts, and the standing finding that pgvector HNSW skips dead index entries — making a live row UNREACHABLE rather than merely slow — means an untuned table degrades recall silently rather than visibly.

dim, embedding_model and mode are set at creation and are NOT castable on update: a changeset attempting to change any of the three is rejected, no path in the context module can alter them, and TC-43.1.3 asserts each one separately.

test_cases.name: a corpus pins its own dimension independent of the tenant pin
preconditions: a tenant whose tenant_embedding_dimension is pinned at 1536
steps: create a corpus with dim 768 and embedding_model nomic-embed-text
insert a chunk and a 768-length vector
expected_results: the vector stores without violating the CHECK
Embeddings.active_dimension/1 for the tenant still returns 1536
articles in the same tenant continue to embed and search at 1536

test_cases.name: a wrong-length vector cannot be stored even bypassing the changeset
steps: insert a document_chunk_embeddings row with a 1536-length vector and dim 768 via raw SQL

test_cases.name: dim, mode and embedding_model are immutable after creation
steps: build an update changeset attempting to change dim
expected_results: each changeset is invalid with an error on the field — silently dropping the change does not satisfy AC-43.1.13
no path in the context module can alter any of the three

test_cases.name: an unsupported dimension is refused at creation
expected_results: the error names the supported set and says a new dimension needs a migration

test_cases.name: tenant isolation on all three tables
preconditions: tenant A and tenant B each with a corpus, chunks and chunk embeddings
steps: as tenant A, list corpora, chunks and embeddings through Loopctl.Repo
expected_results: only tenant A rows are returned from each of the three tables

test_cases.name: chunks are invisible to the article-corpus paths
preconditions: the recall, heat, novelty and consolidation modules on this branch
steps: inspect each for a reference to DocumentChunk or DocumentChunkEmbedding
expected_results: the set of modules inspected is non-empty

test_cases.name: a heavy read joining chunks to embeddings scopes both sources
preconditions: a query joining document_chunks to document_chunk_embeddings
steps: pass it to HeavyRead with a tenant_id
then pass a variant that scopes only the from source
expected_results: the fully scoped query is accepted
the partially scoped variant raises ArgumentError out of HeavyRead.all/2

test_cases.name: corpus delete cascades
preconditions: a corpus with 3 chunks, each with an embedding
expected_results: zero document_chunks rows remain for that corpus

technical_notes: Follow priv/repo/migrations/20260721000100_create_embedding_side_tables.exs closely — it is the reference implementation for an unconstrained vector column with a dim discriminator, and its moduledoc records why each decision was made. The one thing NOT to copy is the live_denorm trigger pair: it exists because article supersession is not expressible across tables, and a document chunk has no supersession state. Note also that RlsHelpers.enable_rls/1's own docstring claims it executes FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and the code does not; trust the code — ENABLE alone is correct here because in production the table owner is schema_admin WITHOUT BYPASSRLS.

locator is jsonb and its INTERNAL shape belongs to the client. loopctl must not validate that it looks like a page number, because the same tier serves a PDF (page), a source file (line range) and an EDI guide (loop and segment). It is stored, returned verbatim, and participates in the idempotency key. Do NOT normalise it — a normalisation that reorders keys changes the idempotency key and silently duplicates every chunk on the next index run.

Because locator is part of the unique index, it must be indexed in a form Postgres can compare deterministically. Store it as jsonb and add the unique index on (corpus_id, source_ref, locator) — jsonb equality is well-defined and key order is normalised by the type itself, which is the one normalisation that is safe precisely because the database does it consistently.

The per-dimension HNSW migration must be a SEPARATE migration file from the table creation, exactly as 20260721000200 is separate from 20260721000100, because CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside the DDL transaction the table creation uses.

AC-43.1.8's guard test is the one most likely to be written vacuously. Anchor it to the modules by name, assert the inspected set is non-empty, and verify it by mutation: temporarily add a reference to DocumentChunk in the recall module and confirm the test fails. A guard that passes against a deliberately broken tree is not a guard.
allow_snippets on the corpus is created in this story but is only ENFORCED in US-43.3, where mode B's snippet policy lives. Creating the column here avoids a second migration on the same table.
Do not add a corpus-level updated-at-driven re-embed path. Re-dimensioning a corpus is delete-and-re-index by design: the source files are the truth and nothing distilled would be lost.

The unique index in AC-43.1.2 puts a jsonb column in a btree, which Postgres allows but caps at ~2704 bytes per index entry; an index insert over that raises. Locators are small in every anticipated use (a page number, a byte range, a heading path), but the migration should note the cap, and if a client ever needs a large locator the fix is a generated locator_hash column in the index rather than widening the entry.

US-43.2's search must reuse index_safe_dimension_knn_base/6 rather than writing a KNN query — the constraint is recorded here because AC-43.1.4's column names are what keep that reuse possible. It emits ONLY the predicates the partial index carries — tenant_id equality, the dimension literal, live_denorm, the cast ORDER BY, and LIMIT — and both the dim literal and the vector typmod are COMPILE-TIME literals, one function clause per supported dimension. That is deliberate: under a Postgres generic plan the planner cannot prove dim = $1 implies dim = 768, so a bound parameter disqualifies the partial index and reverts to a seq scan plus sort. Anything selective added to that inner query is the same regression.
